name: Altman (Nordic TVM)
question: Does trocar-guided anterior transvaginal polypropylene mesh repair improve one-year success over anterior colporrhaphy for symptomatic cystocele?

design.blinding: patients blinded through one year; outcome assessors unblinded

arms.label: Gynecare Prolift anterior transvaginal polypropylene mesh repair

design.population: Women aged at least 18 years with symptomatic primary or recurrent POP-Q stage 2 or higher anterior vaginal wall prolapse who did not need concomitant surgery.
design.locator: NEJM full text, Methods: Patients, Randomization, Study Design; Figure 1

verdictNote: Composite success improved at one year, with more operative and mesh-related harms.
takeaway: Trocar-guided Gynecare Prolift anterior polypropylene mesh repair increased one-year composite anatomic and symptom success versus traditional anterior colporrhaphy (60.8% versus 34.5%); surgery was longer, bleeding and bladder perforation were more frequent, and mesh exposure required reoperation in 3.2%.

reports.label: Urodynamic substudy
reports.citation: Ek M, Tegerstedt G, Falconer C, et al. "Urodynamic assessment of anterior vaginal wall surgery: a randomized comparison between colporraphy and transvaginal mesh." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2010;29(4):527-531. doi:10.1002/nau.20811
reports.followUp: 2 months after surgery; 50-patient randomized urodynamic substudy

results.measure: Change from baseline at 2 months in 23 mesh and 27 colporrhaphy patients
results.note: The abstract gives no numerical pressure change.

reports.label: One-year primary report
reports.citation: Altman D, Väyrynen T, Engh ME, et al. "Anterior Colporrhaphy versus Transvaginal Mesh for Pelvic-Organ Prolapse." *N Engl J Med.* 2011;364(19):1826-1836. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1009521
reports.followUpLocator: NEJM full text, Methods: Study Design; Figure 1

results.measure: One-year POP-Q anterior stage 0 or 1 plus no vaginal bulge; absolute risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Among women with evaluable composite outcomes; 200 and 189 were randomized. Adjusted OR 3.6 (95% CI 2.2–5.9); a missing-data sensitivity analysis still favored mesh.

results.measure: One-year anterior POP-Q stage 0 or 1; absolute risk difference in percentage points
One-year absence of vaginal bulge; absolute risk difference in percentage points

harms.label: New stress urinary incontinence
harms.note: P=0.05; the abstract prints 6.3% for control, but 11/176 rounds to 6.2%.

harms.label: Vaginal wound revision for mesh exposure
harms.note: All six mesh-arm wound revisions corrected exposure; P=0.03.

harms.label: Surgery for stress incontinence by 12 months
Severe pelvic pain at 2 months
harms.note: P=0.22; pain resolved by one year in all but one mesh patient.

delivery.label: Operative technique
delivery.value: Standardized Gynecare Prolift Anterior Pelvic Floor Repair System mesh kit versus standardized traditional anterior colporrhaphy; no concomitant surgery permitted.

delivery.label: Surgeon experience
delivery.value: 58 surgeons at 53 hospitals; median 3 operations of each type per surgeon.

delivery.label: Mean intraoperative blood loss
delivery.note: P<0.001; five mesh patients lost more than 500 mL, including one exceeding 1000 mL.

delivery.label: Perioperative measures
delivery.value: Procedures were standardized; participating surgeons were trained, and postmenopausal patients received topical estrogen before and after surgery.

reports.label: Sponsor-disclosure correction
reports.citation: "Correction: Anterior Colporrhaphy versus Transvaginal Mesh for Pelvic-Organ Prolapse." *N Engl J Med.* 2013;368(4):394. doi:10.1056/NEJMx130001
